errors.english: Accordingly, the word heard indicates that what is being presented here has been recited.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the word 'heard' shows that the speaker is the compiler (saṃgītikāra), as against the Teacher who teaches from his own realization; the English loses the identification of the speaker.

note: A careful, readable rendering of the nidāna commentary; only the point that 'heard' marks the speaker as compiler is blurred.

errors.why: The Tibetan simply says 'this is [called ...]', the name following on the next side; 'untranscribed text' is a processing artifact, not translation.

note: Sound medical rendering of the prameha types; the only real problem is a stray artifact at the end.

errors.english: it is without the subtle and complete syllable (Hum), without vowels, without the moon, and without the (bindu) the drop or point of energy
errors.why: The Tibetan lists the subtle supports of the meditation: a HŪṂ lacking vowel, moon and bindu; a bindu as subtle as a mustard seed; the supremely subtle; or four syllables set in the four cakras; the English makes the HŪṂ itself absent and drops the bindu as subject of 'subtle like a mustard seed'.

errors.english: The term "generation stage" is used here because it is well known to worldly people one line of text regarding the conventional understanding of generation stage.
errors.why: The sentence says the term 'generation stage' here is [not used] in the sense known to worldly people (the negation follows on the next side); 'one line of text regarding the conventional understanding of generation stage' is an artifact, and the English asserts the opposite of the continuing sentence.

fix.find: The term "generation stage" is used here because it is well known to worldly people one line of text regarding the conventional understanding of generation stage.
fix.replace: Here the term "generation stage" is [not used] in the sense familiar to worldly people,

note: The Madhyamaka/Yogācāra and method-tantra argument is broadly right, but the mudrā/subtle-syllable passage is mis-structured and the side ends in a garbled artifact.
Faithful rendering of the arhat and āsrava glosses, with all the correspondences between aggregates, paths and outflows correct.

errors.english: Thus, in the context of the stage of the arisen,
errors.why: རྫོགས་པའི་རིམ་པ is the completion stage, not the generation stage ('stage of the arisen'); the secret initiation is here placed in the completion-stage context.

fix.find: in the context of the stage of the arisen
fix.replace: likewise in the context of the completion stage

errors.english: Depending on the realization that ensues, one will be able to recognize what is pointed out during the master initiation, and the secret, wisdom, and fourth initiations.
errors.why: མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པ here is the abhisamaya (the ritual manual): the initiation, as set out in the abhisamaya, should be understood as characterized by the master, secret, wisdom and fourth initiations, not 'depending on the realization that ensues'.

errors.english: the confluence of the three subtle channels
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of the heart-jewel embodying the combined nature of the three consciousnesses (dependent, imagined, transformed); no channels are mentioned.

errors.english: We also have the statement "followed by the fourth in the same way."
errors.why: The gloss that 'that' (de) refers to the wisdom-knowledge initiation and 'thus' (de bzhin) to thusness is not translated.

note: Readable, but a completion/generation-stage confusion and a few misreadings of the initiation passage need a specialist's correction.
Faithful word-commentary on the wrathful forms, weapons and Vajrapāṇi's proclamation.
Accurate rendering of the benefits of the dharma-eye and the nine knowledges.

errors.english: Some belong to my family [note: the Tathagata family]
errors.why: The speaker is Vajrapāṇi (he says 'I explained seventy million' and, on the next side, 'I am taught as the Vajra family'), so 'my family' is the Vajra family.

fix.replace: [note: the Vajra family; the speaker is Vajrapāṇi]

note: Sound rendering of the homage verses and the family-by-family mantra counts; one misleading note on the speaker's family.
A careful scholarly translation of the four joys and the quoted Hevajra verses, evidently made with the Sanskrit in view.
Faithful rendering of the ten masteries, the three things needing no guarding, and the marks of a great man.
